title: Ajahn Funn: We have come to this meeting – meeting both internally and externally. Having arrived at the monastery, let us all measure and observe…
content:
The Religion Flourishes or Declines Depending on Our Respect for Seven Things

We have come to this meeting – meeting both internally and externally. Having arrived at the monastery, let us all measure and observe our own minds. Is it inside the monastery or outside? For what purpose are we measuring? This very point: we rely on Buddhism. This religion is a tool for alleviating suffering and extinguishing suffering.

The Buddha established the religion within the four assemblies – right here, not elsewhere. What are the four assemblies? Bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs – but at present there are no bhikkhunīs, only bhikkhus, sāmaṇeras, upāsakas, and upāsikās. The religion flourishes depending on these four; the religion declines depending on these four. Why does it decline? Because we do not conduct ourselves or practice in line with the qualities of the Buddha. We have no respect for the qualities of the Buddha, no respect for the qualities of the Dhamma, no respect for the qualities of the Noble Saṅgha, no respect for giving, no respect for virtue, no respect for meditation, no respect for mutual courtesy and hospitality. When we lack respect for these seven things, that causes the religion to decline. If we still have respect for these seven things, the religion will prosper and advance.

title: Ajahn Funn: The Buddha's teaching instructs us to contemplate Buddho so that we know and see clearly the truths of reality (sacca-dhamma). You should all…
content:
When the Mind Is Still in Concentration, It Does Not Die

The Buddha's teaching instructs us to contemplate Buddho so that we know and see clearly the truths of reality (sacca-dhamma). You should all know birth, aging, sickness, and death. This is the real truth. There is also that which is not born, does not age, does not sicken, does not die. We know that this thing is born, this thing ages, this thing sickens, this thing dies. We should contemplate: what is it that is not born, does not age, does not sicken, does not die? Do not think of anything else. Think of our own heart, the one that thinks. Why does it not arise? Because...

We establish concentration: Buddho, Buddho. Our heart stays still within. It does not send out to the front, back, left, right, above, or below. It stays fixed right in the middle. The knower remains still. Then it does not die. When it is still like that, it does not die and it does not arise. Not arising, it does not age. Not aging, it does not sicken. Not sickening, it does not die. Not dying, it surely does not suffer. What do you say to that? We must look here. Right now we are being born — sitting here, we are being born without stopping. Even while listening to this sermon, it hasn't stopped.

title: Ajahn Funn: The country is not good, it’s chaotic. Look at the earth, sky, weather, mountains, and forests – they don’t have any problem. Sit…
content:
When the Mind Is Not Good, Everything Is Not Good – Family, Nation, All Are in Turmoil

The country is not good, it’s chaotic. Look at the earth, sky, weather, mountains, and forests – they don’t have any problem. Sit and look. Whatever we do for a living ends in loss and ruin. Seeking anything brings suffering and hardship. What suffers? What is difficult? Is it possessions, money, gold? What suffers? What is difficult? Sit and look. In the past we had no opportunity to make merit and wholesome qualities. Now we can do it fully, completely. Look – what hinders you? What lacks or falls short? Learn to examine your own heart. The reason for loss and ruin is this: our mind is not good. When our mind is not good, we are miserable, troubled, turbulent, and distressed. When the mind is like this, it causes loss and ruin. When the mind is not good, whatever you do is not good, whatever you seek is not good, your work is not good, your livelihood is not good, your government service is not good, your business is not good, your family is not good, your neighbors and marketplace and nation are not good. Your mind is just not good. Look – husband and wife quarrel. The mind is not good. What do you say? Look. Look so that you know. This is because of this cause.

title: Ajahn Funn: What does it mean to abandon defilement? When we’re stained with craving—hankering and restless—the mind abandons it all. Passion, delight, and desire for…
content:
The Four Visions That Inspired the Buddha: Birth, Aging, Illness, Death

What does it mean to abandon defilement? When we’re stained with craving—hankering and restless—the mind abandons it all. Passion, delight, and desire for things: It abandons them all. Greed: It abandons it all. Aversion, anger: It abandons it all. Delusion, ignorance: It abandons it all. Becoming and birth: It abandons them all. It enters the “land” of unbinding, having disbanded suffering and stress in the cycles of wandering-on, and won’t come swimming back to dying and taking rebirth ever again.

This is why I want you to understand the practice. The Buddha set out the religion because he was afraid that we’d meet with things that aren’t good, that we’d be worried and possessive about this, that, or the other thing—but those things don’t help us gain release from suffering. So don’t let yourself get worried and possessive. Place your heart in the Buddha, in Buddho, as your refuge. Be constantly alert—sitting, standing, walking, lying down. Be mindful. Abyākatā dhammā: Make your mind Buddho. Make your mind serene, happy, and at ease.

Buddho is a mind fully serene. Bright. Clear. One who knows all knowable things, thoroughly and throughout; one who knows birth, aging, illness, and death; one who knows all suffering; one who knows kamma and animosity. This is why we say that the Lord Buddha awakened to all noble dhammas (ariya-dhamma).

How was he able to let go? Because the four visions inspired his heart. Which four visions? Birth, aging, illness, and death: That’s what he saw that enabled him to abandon his royal treasures without taking any delight in them. That’s what happened—nothing else far away. If he had held onto his royal treasures, he wouldn’t have been able to escape these four things.

title: Ajahn Funn: He contemplated using the three kinds of knowledge (ñāṇa): 1. Pubbenivāsānussati-ñāṇa – knowledge of recollecting past lives. He contemplated the planes of existence…
content:
The Buddha’s Three Knowledges: Past Lives, Passing Away and Arising, Ending of Influxes

He contemplated using the three kinds of knowledge (ñāṇa):

1. Pubbenivāsānussati-ñāṇa – knowledge of recollecting past lives. He contemplated the planes of existence – whatever he had been born as, in whatever realm or plane, he knew completely, knowing successively back and back until no origin could be found. That is why he was courageous and able to establish the Dispensation.

2. The second knowledge: Cutūpapāta-ñāṇa – knowledge of the passing away and arising of beings. When we pass away from here, where will we be reborn? The Buddha knew completely. Whoever had done what, whoever was a peta, an animal, a hell-being, a celestial being, a god, or a Brahmā – he knew completely. He taught that this meditation is the path; he taught that this concentration and wisdom (samādhi-paññā) is the way of practice.

3. The third knowledge: Āsavakkhaya-ñāṇa – knowledge of the destruction of the influxes. Those who are free from the influxes, defilements, becomings, and births – he knew. The Buddha knew the 84,000 Dhamma aggregates contained in the three Piṭakas: the Suttanta Piṭaka, Vinaya Piṭaka, and Paramattha Piṭaka.

title: Ajahn Funn: We come to the monastery to weigh and see: which is greater, happiness or suffering? Which is greater, good or evil? We come…
content:
Wholesome Mind (Kusala): Peaceful, Light, Happy, and at Ease

We come to the monastery to weigh and see: which is greater, happiness or suffering? Which is greater, good or evil? We come to the monastery to listen to Dhamma. Listen and see: right now, in what Dhamma, in what realm, in what plane of existence is your mind? Come to know it. Whether your mind is in kusala (wholesome) or akusala (unwholesome), know it. Recite "Buddho, Buddho" and focus on looking at your mind. If your mind is kusala, what is it like? The mind is peaceful. It does not send itself forwards, backwards, left, right, above, or below. It stays right in the middle, the knower: "Buddho, Buddho". The mind is calm, cool, happy, and at ease. Kāya-lahutā – lightness of the body; citta-lahutā – lightness of mind. The mind is light, the body is light. Not heavy, not sluggish, not drowsy, not lonely. Suffering disappears, hardship disappears, trouble and annoyance disappear. At ease in body and mind. That is the genuine merit, genuine wholesomeness – there is no other merit. That is genuine happiness, genuine comfort. This will become our merit, our vāsanā, our pāramī, our habitual tendency, sticking to us and carrying us on to every life and every birth. Understand this.

title: Ajahn Funn: The four elements – earth, water, fire, wind – come together. The earth element: hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, tendons, bones,…
content:
The Four Elements: Earth, Water, Wind, Fire – Coming Together as a Person

The four elements – earth, water, fire, wind – come together. The earth element: hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, tendons, bones, liver, kidneys, small intestine, large intestine, old food, new food – whatever is hard in our body is called the earth element. The water element: bile, phlegm, sweat, lymph, mucus, saliva – whatever is liquid in our body is called the water element. The wind element: in-breath, out-breath, wind moving upward, wind moving downward, wind moving throughout the body – that is classed as the wind element. The fire element: that which warms our body, digests food, or ages and deteriorates the body – that is called the fire element.

When these four come together, it's called a person, a self. When there is a self, everyone has the four elements, the five aggregates, and the six sense spheres together. So why are people not the same? Some are low, some are dark or fair, some are big, some are small – not the same, not equal. Why? For this reason: they differ in virtue and qualities. This is it: we lack action.

title: Ajahn Funn: Why come see? Because we hold this to be self, to be a being, a person, a "me" or "him." Let us see…
content:
The Body Bounded by Skin, Filled with Impurities – Hair, Nails, Teeth, Skin

Why come see? Because we hold this to be self, to be a being, a person, a "me" or "him." Let us see whether it really is a self or a being, whether it really is a person. Where is the person? Is this "me" the person? Or are the hairs the person? Or the nails? Or the teeth? Or the skin? No, aren't they? Or is it the flesh? Or the bones? Or the liver, kidneys, small intestine, large intestine? Those are just names. Where is the person? We must know and see this. This is the point: let us all know kammaṭṭhāna. This is to see rūpa-dhamma and nāma-dhamma. The concocter, the fabricator — that is thinking, intending, mental objects, perceptions — that is nāma-dhamma, merely thinking and intending. Bring this to contemplation. Know "na" and know "mo". Only then can we protect our heart. If we do not know "na" and "mo", we cannot protect our heart.

The teaching says: Now, where are we a person? Tacapariyanto — bounded by skin all around. Pūrāṇānappakārassa asucino — filled with all kinds of impurities. Atthi imasmiṃ kāye — in this body. They do not say that other body; "this body" means pointing to each one of our own bodies. Filled with impurities.

title: Ajahn Funn: That is why we are taught to go to the temple. Nowadays, people don’t examine themselves at all. They are completely in the…
content:
Peace Is Happiness: There Is No Happiness Equal to Peace

That is why we are taught to go to the temple. Nowadays, people don’t examine themselves at all. They are completely in the dark. Therefore, they kill, slash, and stab each other without thinking of their own selves. Their own selves fear death; others also fear death. So don’t do it. If everyone knew this and practiced this, everyone would be at ease, the town would be peaceful, the country would be peaceful, the human world would be peaceful. Peace is happiness. There is no happiness equal to peace.

Therefore, from now on, perform this regular practice: go to the temple every day. Go to the temple and listen to Dhamma every day. Buddho, Dhammo, Saṅgho – our refuges are only these. Nothing else can be relied upon at all. If you know this, remember it. Go to the temple every day. Contemplate yourself so that you see within. See what is good, what is bad, what is happiness, what is suffering. When you see, doubt ends, and you have only confidence in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Sangha. Then you have a refuge, a shelter. There is nothing in the world like it.

title: Ajahn Funn: Knowing this, quickly correct it right now. Don't let it pass even a moment. If you leave what is bad in place, then…
content:
The Root of All Good and Bad Is the Heart – Like the Root of a Tree

Knowing this, quickly correct it right now. Don't let it pass even a moment. If you leave what is bad in place, then you will remain a bad person. This is it. People blame this and that as bad, doing this is bad, doing that is bad. Why is it bad? We don't look at its origin. We don't look at its root. Where does the root come from? If the root is not good, how can the tip be good? We must look at its root – that is, this heart. This is the root. If the root is good, the fruit will be good. It's like a tree: if you take good care of the root, fertilize and water it well, the tree will be good, producing abundant flowers and fruit. The same here. If our heart is good, then everything we do becomes good. Whatever livelihood we pursue becomes good: trade, government service, family, relatives, neighbors, the country – all good. Whether ordained or not, if the heart is good, there will be no quarrels, no distress, only peace.
